1.title: Authentication in Microsoft Entra ID
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Authentication in Microsoft Entra I D. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft Entra. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Describe the authentication methods. Describe multifactor authentication. Describe password protection and management capabilities. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft Entra (twenty-five to thirty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Authentication methods
1.text: Authentication methods. Microsoft Entra I D supports several ways to prove who you are. They range from weak (password only) to strong (passwordless and phishing-resistant). Password. What it is: Something you know. Strength: Weakest: can be guessed, phished or reused. Microsoft Authenticator app. What it is: Approve a push notification or enter a code; can be passwordless. Strength: Strong. Windows Hello for Business. What it is: P I N or biometric tied to the device; passwordless. Strength: Strong. fido two security key. What it is: A physical key (U S B or N F C). Strength: Strongest: phishing-resistant. Passkey. What it is: A cryptographic key pair stored on a device or key; phishing-resistant. Strength: Strong.

1.title: Authentication methods, continued
1.text: Authentication methods. Certificate-based authentication. What it is: Sign in with a certificate. Strength: Strong. O A T H tokens. What it is: Hardware or software code generators. Strength: Medium. S M S and voice call. What it is: A code by text or call. Strength: Weaker: can be intercepted or S I M-swapped. Temporary Access Pass. What it is: A time-limited code to set up passwordless methods. Strength: For onboarding and recovery.

1.title: Authentication methods, continued
1.text: Authentication methods. The figure shows this: Authentication methods from weakest to strongest.

1.title: Authentication methods, continued
1.text: Authentication methods. Passwordless means signing in without typing a password: the user proves possession of a device and (usually) a biometric or P I N. It is more secure (nothing to phish) and easier. Exam tip: Strongest and phishing-resistant: fido two keys, passkeys, Windows Hello for Business, certificate-based authentication. Weakest second factors: S M S and voice. Passwordless removes the password entirely.

1.title: Multifactor authentication (MFA)
1.text: Multifactor authentication. M F A requires two or more different factor types, so a stolen password alone is not enough. Something you know. Password, P I N. Something you have. Phone with Authenticator, security key. Something you are. Fingerprint, face. A password plus a P I N is not M F A (both are knowledge). M F A blocks over ninety-nine percent of account compromise attacks according to Microsoft.

1.title: Ways to require MFA
1.text: Ways to require M F A. Security defaults. Free, preset protections that require M F A for all users and block legacy sign-in; good for small organizations. Conditional Access policy. Flexible rules: require M F A under conditions (module five); needs P one. Per-user M F A. The older way to enable M F A user by user.

1.title: Ways to require MFA, continued
1.text: Ways to require M F A. The figure shows this: M F A combines two different factors, such as a password and an app approval. Exam tip: M F A equals two different factor types. Security defaults equals simplest, free. Conditional Access equals most flexible ("require M F A when the user is outside the office"). Push fatigue attacks are reduced by number matching in Authenticator.

1.title: Password protection and management
1.text: Password protection and management. Microsoft Entra Password Protection. Blocks weak and commonly used passwords: a global banned password list maintained by Microsoft plus a custom banned list (for example company names); can be extended on-premises with agents. Smart lockout. Locks out attackers after repeated failures but keeps legitimate users working by telling them apart. Self-service password reset (S S P R). Users reset or change their own password after proving identity, which cuts help desk calls. Password writeback. Sends a reset password back to on-premises A D in a hybrid setup. Passwordless. The best way to avoid password problems.

1.title: Password protection and management, continued
1.text: Password protection and management. Modern password guidance: length matters more than complexity, do not reuse passwords, check against banned lists and use M F A. Exam tip: Banned password list equals blocks weak passwords. Smart lockout equals stops guessing without locking out real users. S S P R equals users fix their own password. Password writeback equals needed so S S P R works with on-premises A D.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants the most phishing-resistant sign-in method for administrators. Which should it choose? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A fido two security key. fido two keys are phishing-resistant and among the strongest methods.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user signs in with a password and then a P I N. Why is this not M F A? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Both are something you know. M F A needs two different factor types, and a password and a P I N are both knowledge factors.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A small business wants free, preset protections that require M F A for everyone. What should it enable? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Security defaults. Security defaults are free preset protections that include M F A for all users.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which feature stops people from choosing passwords such as "Password one hundred twenty-three"? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Microsoft Entra Password Protection. Password Protection blocks weak and commonly used passwords with banned lists.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Users forget passwords often and the help desk is overloaded. Which capability helps most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Self-service password reset. S S P R lets users reset their own passwords after proving who they are.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A sign-in method that uses no password and relies on a device plus a biometric or P I N is called what? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Passwordless authentication. Signing in without a password using a device and a biometric or P I N is passwordless.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which methods are phishing-resistant? Answer: fido two security keys, passkeys, Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication. Question two. Which second factors are the weakest? Answer: S M S and voice calls. Question three. What does M F A require? Answer: Two or more different factor types.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are security defaults? Answer: Free preset protections that require M F A and block legacy sign-in. Question five. What does smart lockout do? Answer: Locks out attackers after failures while keeping legitimate users working. Question six. What is S S P R? Answer: Self-service password reset: users reset their own passwords.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Methods: password (weakest), Authenticator, Windows Hello, fido two, passkeys, certificates, O A T H, S M S and voice, Temporary Access Pass. Passwordless: no password typed; device plus P I N or biometric; phishing-resistant options. M F A: two different factor types; ways: security defaults, Conditional Access, per-user M F A. Passwords: Password Protection (banned lists), smart lockout, S S P R, password writeback. In the next module, we continue the course.
